subtopics.title: Reading a Formula Like a Sentence

questions.question: In cost = R380 + R9,50 × km, the R380 represents:
options: The fixed charge, owed regardless of distance

questions.question: The R9,50 in the formula is:
options: The rate — the amount each kilometre adds to the bill

questions.question: In this formula, cost is called the DEPENDENT variable because:
options: The cost depends on the distance driven

subtopics.title: Forward Substitution — Pricing the 260 km Trip

questions.question: The cost of a 260 km trip is:
A student computes (380 + 9,50) × 260 = R101 270. What went wrong?
options: Order of operations — multiplication must happen before addition

questions.question: Why should the formula and the substitution line be set out before calculating?
options: Each line typically earns its own mark and lets the marker follow your method
It makes the page look full

questions.question: Which sense check confirms R2 850 is plausible for the 260 km trip?
options: The driving charge (R2 470) should far exceed the fixed fee (R380) on a long trip — and it does

subtopics.title: Reverse Substitution — How Far Does R1 900 Go?

questions.question: With a budget of R1 900, the first step after substituting is:
options: Subtract the R380 fixed charge from both sides, leaving R1 520 for driving
Add the R380 to the budget

questions.question: R1 900 buys a trip of:
Dividing the whole R1 900 by R9,50 gives 200 km. Why is this wrong?
options: R380 of the budget pays the fixed fee and never buys kilometres — it must be removed first

questions.question: How is the answer of 160 km verified?
options: Substitute forwards: 380 + 9,50 × 160 = R1 900, exactly the budget

subtopics.title: The General Method, the Classic Traps, and Where This Skill Lives

questions.question: The correct unwinding order for reverse substitution in a fixed-plus-rate formula is:
options: Divide by the rate first, then subtract the fixed part
Subtract the fixed part first, then divide by the rate

questions.question: A formula requires kilometres but the question gives 3 500 metres. You should:
When should rounding happen in a multi-step substitution?
options: Only at the final answer — carry full values through the working

subtopics.title: The Gate Fee and the Meter

questions.question: In the soccer-match comparison, the R380 hire charge plays the part of:
options: The gate fee paid once at the entrance

questions.question: Which clue in the formula tells you R9,50 is the repeating charge?
options: It is multiplied by the kilometres, so it is charged once for every kilometre
It has a comma in it

questions.question: Which everyday bill has the SAME skeleton as this formula?
options: A plumber's call-out fee plus an hourly rate

questions.question: Why are the kilometres called the independent variable?
options: They are always bigger than the cost
You choose them freely, and the cost answers back

subtopics.title: Running the Machine Forwards — and the R101 270 Disaster

questions.question: 260 kilometres at R9,50 each comes to:
In plain words, what does adding R380 to R9,50 BEFORE multiplying actually do?
options: It charges the R380 gate fee once for every one of the 260 kilometres

questions.question: 260 × R380 = R98 800. What is this amount in the wrong answer of R101 270?
options: The phantom gate fees that were never charged

questions.question: What makes R2 850 a believable bakkie-hire bill?
options: Most of it is driving (R2 470) with a small admin charge on top

subtopics.title: Running It Backwards — R1 900 in Your Pocket

questions.question: Out of a R1 900 budget, how much can actually turn into kilometres?
The wrong answer of 200 km is exactly 40 km too far. Where do those 40 km come from?
options: R380 divided by R9,50 — the fixed fee spent as if it bought driving

questions.question: Why is 'shoes off before socks' a good picture for reverse substitution?
options: You undo the steps in the opposite order from how they were done

questions.question: Running 160 km back through the formula gives 380 + 9,50 × 160 = R1 900. This shows that:
options: The answer lands exactly on the budget given, so it is proven correct
